material_systems.name: Self-Etching Primer (Phosphoric Acid + Zinc)

primer.type: Self-etching primer — phosphoric acid etches Al2O3 oxide layer, zinc chromate provides galvanic corrosion resistance
products: Sherwin-Williams Wash Primer / Vinyl Wash Primer
primer.notes: MANDATORY for ALL aluminum siding repaints. Self-etching chemistry is the ONLY primer class that bonds to aluminum's Al2O3 oxide layer. STIX-class adhesion primers (for vinyl/PVC) do NOT work on aluminum oxide — different chemistry entirely. DFT MUST be held to 0.5-1.0 mils — excessive thickness (>1.0 mil) causes COHESIVE FAILURE within the primer film. The acid-etch reaction zone has limited depth; primer beyond that zone has no bond substrate. Single coat only. Fine-atomization spray tips required. Single-pass technique — do not double-back. High coverage rate (500 SF/gal) reflects the intentionally thin film build.

applies_when.condition: always — self-etching primer is mandatory regardless of substrate state or quality tier

material_systems.notes: Single primer system for aluminum. No state-dependent primer branching — both states require the same self-etching chemistry. Primer serves adhesion AND corrosion resistance functions. The zinc component provides galvanic protection of the aluminum substrate. Coverage rate is higher than typical exterior primers because the film must be intentionally thin (0.5-1.0 mil vs 1.5-2.5 mil for standard primers).

material_systems.name: Epoxy Intermediate Primer (Coastal Conditional)

intermediate.type: Two-component epoxy primer — chemical-resistant barrier between self-etching primer and acrylic topcoat
intermediate.notes: CONDITIONAL — applies ONLY when site environment = coastal/marine (salt-air exposure zone). Creates a three-layer system: self-etch primer -> epoxy intermediate -> acrylic topcoat. The epoxy layer provides a chemical-resistant barrier that standard acrylic topcoats cannot provide alone in salt-laden environments. Salt air penetrates through acrylic topcoat to the primer-metal interface, initiating galvanic corrosion. Must verify inter-coat compatibility with self-etching primer below and acrylic finish above — product-specific PDS verification required.

applies_when.condition: CONDITIONAL — only when site assessment indicates marine/harsh coastal salt-air exposure

material_systems.notes: Adds one coat to the system. Coastal variant total coat stack: QT2 = 3 coats (self-etch + epoxy + 1 finish), QT3 = 4 coats (self-etch + epoxy + 2 finish). Non-coastal projects skip this system entirely.

material_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Exterior Latex — All Colors

finish.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior latex for ALL colors. No LRV restriction on aluminum — aluminum conducts heat efficiently, no thermal warping risk at any color. Any LRV is permissible. Acrylic latex binder is the standard for exterior durability and flexibility. Alkyd finish over self-etch primer is technically acceptable but uncommon in residential — acrylic provides better long-term flexibility and color retention. Coverage rate reflects smooth, non-porous metal substrate over primed surface.

applies_when.condition: always — single finish system for all colors

material_systems.notes: Single finish system. Unlike vinyl repaint (which splits into standard and IR-reflective finish systems by LRV class), aluminum repaint has ONE finish system for all colors. This is a significant simplification. Dark colors are fully permissible — aluminum's thermal conductivity dissipates heat. Melting point (1220 degrees F) is vastly above any solar-gain temperature.

SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT.notes: Sound factory-baked enamel or previously painted aluminum. Non-porous metal surface provides very consistent coverage. High rate reflects intentionally thin film build (0.5-1.0 mil DFT). Use mid-range for standard conditions.

SS_EXT_CHALKING.notes: Chalking aluminum after complete chalk removal and oxide scuff. Surface is slightly more open after scuff than sound-paint state. Chalk MUST be fully removed before priming — any remaining chalk causes bond failure. Lower end of range accounts for freshly exposed aluminum absorbing slightly more primer at scuff sites.

assumptions: Full-surface coverage required — self-etching primer must contact aluminum oxide across entire surface.
Coverage based on NET siding area from PaintScope (PS_EXT_SURFACE_SF.SIDING_FIELD).
Single coat only. Do NOT double-coat self-etching primer — DFT above 1.0 mil causes cohesive failure.
Coverage rates are higher than standard exterior primers because film is intentionally thin (0.5-1.0 mil vs 1.5-2.5 mil typical).

SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT.notes: Epoxy intermediate over self-etching primer on aluminum. Standard epoxy coverage on primed metal.

SS_EXT_CHALKING.notes: Same coverage — epoxy is applied over self-etching primer, not directly to aluminum. Substrate state does not affect epoxy coverage.

assumptions: Applied over cured self-etching primer, not directly to aluminum.
Coverage based on NET siding area from PaintScope.

lap_horizontal.notes: Standard aluminum lap siding. Smooth factory profile over primed surface. Best coverage rate. Aluminum lap profiles are shallower than vinyl — tighter tolerances in factory forming.

board_and_batten.notes: Aluminum board-and-batten profile. Effective area ~1.08-1.12x net due to batten profiles. Less deep than wood equivalent (1.20x).

shake_shingle.notes: Aluminum shake/shingle panels. Textured surface with many edges increases material consumption ~10-12% vs smooth lap. Less pronounced texture than vinyl shake equivalent.

assumptions: Coverage is per NET siding area from PaintScope.
Primed surface (self-etching primer coat applied) provides consistent base for acrylic topcoat.
QT2 = single coat. QT3 = two coats (multiply gallon estimate by coat count).
Aluminum siding profiles are generally smoother/shallower than vinyl equivalents — slightly better coverage per profile type.
No dutch_lap profile — aluminum siding was not manufactured in dutch lap style (wood and vinyl only).

consumables.name: Airless spray tips — fine-atomization 311-413 for primer, 413-515 for finish
consumables.notes: CRITICAL: Self-etching primer requires fine-atomization tips (311-413) to achieve 0.5-1.0 mil DFT target. Standard tips over-apply. 413-515 tip for acrylic finish coat (normal atomization). Replace when fan pattern deteriorates. Separate tips for primer and finish — do not cross-contaminate.

consumables.name: Airless sprayer filters (gun and manifold)
consumables.notes: Gun filter and manifold filter. Clean thoroughly between self-etching primer and finish coat — primer chemistry is incompatible with acrylic finish if cross-contaminated. Replace when clogging causes pressure spikes.

consumables.name: Brushes 2-3 inch for J-channel detail and cut-in
consumables.notes: 2 inch for J-channels and under-sill channels. 3 inch for siding-to-trim cut-in. QT3 detail work only. Use separate brushes for primer and finish.

consumables.name: Wet film thickness gauge / dry film thickness gauge
consumables.notes: CRITICAL for self-etching primer DFT verification. Wet film gauge used during application to spot-check. Dry film gauge (magnetic type for ferrous-compatible, or eddy current for aluminum) for QC verification after cure. DFT must be 0.5-1.0 mil — over-application causes cohesive failure. This consumable is unique to aluminum siding — not needed for vinyl or wood siding specs.

consumables.name: TSP cleaner / alkaline aluminum siding wash concentrate
consumables.notes: Trisodium phosphate or dedicated aluminum siding cleaner concentrate. Mix per manufacturer directions. Required for chalk, mildew, and dirt removal. For heavy chalk: increase concentration and dwell time per manufacturer instructions. Alkaline cleaner neutralizes chalk and lifts oxidation products.

consumables.name: Pressure washer tips (25-40 degree fan)
consumables.notes: 25-degree tip for siding field wash. 40-degree for delicate areas (J-channels, corners). 1000-1500 PSI — aluminum is more durable than vinyl (no behind-panel water infiltration risk at higher pressure), but do not exceed 2000 PSI to avoid denting thin-gauge panels.

consumables.name: Synthetic steel wool / 180-320 grit abrasive pads
consumables.notes: 180-320 grit abrasive pads or synthetic steel wool for oxide layer scuffing. This is MORE aggressive than vinyl scuff — purpose is to mechanically break the Al2O3 oxide film, not just create adhesion tooth. Higher usage rate (1 per 150 SF vs 1 per 200 SF for vinyl) reflects the harder oxide layer. Do NOT use real steel wool — ferrous particles embed in aluminum and cause galvanic corrosion (rust spots).

consumables.name: Siliconized acrylic exterior caulk
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: QT3 only. Paintable siliconized acrylic for siding-to-trim joints. Aluminum has minimal thermal movement at joints compared to vinyl or wood — polyurethane not required. Estimate 50-100 LF per typical residential project.

consumables.name: Masking tape (exterior grade UV-resistant)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum. Blue tape for trim transitions. Red stucco poly tape (30-day UV) for extended spray masking. Aluminum siding projects may run multi-day — UV-resistant rating is important.

consumables.name: Masking paper / kraft paper 12-18 inch
consumables.notes: For masking windows, doors, and trim during spray application. Paper + tape machine application for speed. Used for ext_trim_mask and ext_roofline_mask zones.

consumables.name: Pre-taped masking film (hand-masker rolls)
consumables.notes: Pre-taped plastic film for window and door masking during spray. Faster than paper + tape for full-cover window and door masking. Used for ext_window_mask and ext_door_mask zones.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 4 mil
consumables.notes: Landscape, hardscape, and HVAC/utility protection during spray and wash. 4 mil minimum — thinner tears on shrubs and rough surfaces. Also protects from wash runoff containing chalk residue and alkaline cleaner — more runoff than vinyl wash.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloths
consumables.notes: Reusable canvas drops along foundation perimeter for drip protection during wash and spray. Chalk-laden wash runoff stains concrete — drop cloths at foundation line help contain runoff.

compatibility_rules.description: Self-etching primer ALWAYS required — no skip-prime option
compatibility_rules.notes: MANDATORY. Standard exterior primers, bonding primers, and STIX-class adhesion primers (for vinyl) do NOT bond to aluminum's Al2O3 oxide layer. Self-etching primer (phosphoric acid + zinc) is the ONLY primer that chemically bonds to aluminum. No exceptions, no substitution.

compatibility_rules.description: DFT of self-etching primer MUST be 0.5-1.0 mil — over-application = HARD STOP
compatibility_rules.notes: CRITICAL. Self-etching primer applied above 1.0 mil DFT fails cohesively WITHIN the primer film. The acid-etch reaction zone has limited depth — primer beyond that zone has no bond substrate. This is a UNIQUE failure mode: more primer = worse bond (opposite of all other primer systems). DFT gauge verification is required during and after application.

compatibility_rules.description: Coastal environment triggers epoxy intermediate layer
compatibility_rules.notes: CONDITIONAL. In marine/harsh coastal environments, salt-air penetrates standard acrylic topcoat to the primer-metal interface. Epoxy intermediate provides chemical-resistant barrier. Three-layer system. Non-coastal projects skip epoxy entirely.
Standard path. Self-etching primer + acrylic topcoat. No epoxy intermediate needed in non-coastal environments.

compatibility_rules.description: Chalk must be fully removed before primer — mandatory gate
compatibility_rules.notes: MANDATORY GATE. Residual chalk powder acts as a bond-breaker — self-etching primer acid cannot reach aluminum through chalk residue. Chalk verification applies to ALL substrate states including SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (verification confirms no hidden chalk). Any white transfer on dark cloth = re-wash required.

compatibility_rules.description: No alkyd/oil finish on aluminum — acrylic only recommended

then.reason: Alkyd/oil finishes over self-etching primer are technically possible but NOT recommended for residential exterior. Acrylic latex provides superior long-term flexibility, color retention, and UV resistance. Alkyd adhesion to self-etching primer layer is inferior to acrylic. Use 100% acrylic exterior latex only.

compatibility_rules.notes: STRONG RECOMMENDATION. Unlike vinyl (where alkyd is a HARD STOP due to thermal movement), aluminum does not have thermal expansion concerns. However, acrylic is the standard and strongly preferred.
Economy tier. Single finish coat over self-etching primer (or over epoxy intermediate in coastal variant). Acceptable for budget-constrained work, rental property, pre-sale cosmetic refresh.

compatibility_rules.description: QT3 — two finish coats + detail work + caulk assessment
compatibility_rules.notes: Standard residential tier. Two finish coats for full hide, proper film build, and maximum durability. Brush detail at J-channels, under-sill channels, and trim cut-in. Caulk assessment at siding-to-trim joints.

compatibility_rules.description: No LRV restriction — any color permitted on aluminum
compatibility_rules.notes: NO RESTRICTION. Unlike vinyl siding (LRV <35 hard stop, LRV 35-55 requires IR-reflective), aluminum conducts heat efficiently. No thermal warping risk. No IR-reflective product requirement. Any color, any LRV is fully permissible. Melting point (1220 degrees F) vastly exceeds any surface temperature from solar gain.

then.reason: Dented, bent, or punctured aluminum panels should be straightened or replaced before painting. Painting over dented panels traps moisture in deformations and creates differential expansion stress at dent edges. Severely damaged panels are replacement scope, not painting scope.

compatibility_rules.notes: Unlike vinyl (HARD_STOP on physical damage), minor aluminum dents can be painted over with documented risk acceptance. Severe damage is replacement scope.

compatibility_rules.description: No steel wool on aluminum — synthetic pads only

then.reason: Real steel wool leaves ferrous particles embedded in aluminum surface. These particles cause galvanic corrosion (iron-aluminum galvanic cell), producing rust spots under the coating. Use ONLY synthetic steel wool or synthetic abrasive pads.

compatibility_rules.notes: ABSOLUTE CONSTRAINT. Ferrous contamination of aluminum is irreversible without aggressive chemical treatment. Synthetic pads only.

risk_notes.description: Self-etching primer applied above 1.0 mil DFT fails cohesively WITHIN the primer film. The acid-etch reaction creates a bond zone of limited depth. Primer beyond that zone has no bond substrate — it splits at the bond-zone boundary under thermal cycling or mechanical stress. This is unique to self-etching chemistry: more primer = worse bond.
risk_notes.mitigation: Strict DFT control: 0.5-1.0 mil ONLY. Fine-atomization spray tips (311-413). Single-pass technique. Wet film gauge during application. Dry film gauge QC after cure. Train applicators specifically on this failure mode.

risk_notes.topic: Chalk-induced peeling — residual chalk as bond-breaker
risk_notes.description: Residual chalk powder on aluminum surface prevents self-etching primer acid from contacting metal. Primer bonds to loose chalk layer instead of aluminum. Entire coating system peels at chalk interface within 12-24 months, concentrated on south/west facades where original chalking was most severe.
risk_notes.mitigation: Mandatory chalk verification gate. Pressure wash with TSP/alkaline cleaner. Hand-rub test with dark cloth after drying. Re-wash if any chalk transfers. Multiple passes for heavy chalk. Document verification in QC log.

risk_notes.topic: Wrong primer substitution — non-self-etching primer on aluminum
risk_notes.description: Standard exterior primers, bonding primers, and STIX-class adhesion primers do NOT bond to aluminum oxide. They sit on the surface without chemical reaction. Entire coating system peels in sheets within first thermal cycle season. This is a material specification error.
risk_notes.mitigation: Lock primer specification to self-etching type containing phosphoric acid and zinc. QC verification at material delivery — check product label and PDS for self-etching designation. STIX-class primers are NOT equivalent. Do NOT accept substitutions.

risk_notes.topic: Oxide reformation — delayed priming after surface prep
risk_notes.description: Aluminum re-oxidizes rapidly after oxide layer is mechanically broken by scuffing. If self-etching primer is not applied within 4-8 hours (2-4 hours coastal/humid), reformed oxide reduces primer bond quality. Extended delays (24+ hours) may result in insufficient primer adhesion.
risk_notes.mitigation: Schedule scuffing and priming as sequential same-day tasks. In coastal/humid environments, reduce window to 2-4 hours. If delay unavoidable, re-scuff before priming. SOP should enforce same-day scuff-to-prime sequencing.

risk_notes.description: In marine/harsh coastal environments, salt air penetrates standard acrylic topcoat to the primer-metal interface. Without epoxy intermediate barrier, salt initiates galvanic corrosion beneath the coating. Blistering and peeling result, concentrated on windward facades. Onset 2-5 years.
risk_notes.mitigation: Coastal environment trigger enforced by COMPAT_ALRP_003. Three-layer system: self-etch -> epoxy -> acrylic. Verify coastal classification during site assessment.

risk_notes.description: Real steel wool leaves ferrous particles embedded in aluminum surface. Iron-aluminum galvanic cell produces rust spots under the coating that bleed through. Contamination is irreversible without aggressive chemical treatment.
risk_notes.mitigation: HARD STOP on steel wool. Use ONLY synthetic steel wool or synthetic abrasive pads. QC verification of prep materials at job site.

risk_notes.topic: Wash runoff from chalk removal staining hardscape
risk_notes.description: Alkaline cleaner + chalk residue in wash runoff can stain concrete driveways, patios, and walkways. Staining is more pronounced than vinyl wash runoff due to heavier chalk load and stronger cleaner concentration.
risk_notes.mitigation: Drop cloths and plastic sheeting over hardscape in wash zone. Pre-wet hardscape before washing siding. Neutralize alkaline runoff with water rinse of hardscape after siding wash complete.

assumptions.value: 500 SF/gal baseline for self-etching primer on aluminum — intentionally thin film (0.5-1.0 mil DFT)
assumptions.note: High coverage rate reflects thin-film requirement. Research notes suggest 400-500 SF/gal; using 500 as baseline with 400-600 range for conservative estimation. Lower end for chalking-state surfaces after scuff.

assumptions.value: 375 SF/gal baseline on smooth aluminum over primed surface
assumptions.note: Aluminum is smooth, non-porous metal — similar coverage to primed vinyl lap siding. Slightly lower than vinyl standard (400 SF/gal) because aluminum profiles have more defined edges and seams.

assumptions.value: 325 SF/gal for epoxy intermediate coat on primed aluminum
assumptions.source: Research RF-007; standard epoxy primer coverage rates from manufacturer PDS
assumptions.note: No doctrine-level specification for epoxy intermediate coverage. Derived from standard two-component epoxy primer PDS data. Conservative estimate. Epoxy is thicker-build than self-etching primer.

assumptions.value: Aluminum siding was not manufactured in dutch lap profile — excluded from coverage_by_profile
assumptions.source: Researcher analysis — aluminum siding product history
assumptions.note: Aluminum siding was primarily manufactured in lap horizontal, board-and-batten, and shake/shingle profiles. Dutch lap is a vinyl/wood profile.

assumptions.value: RRP/lead-safe consumables excluded — aluminum siding factory-baked enamel was never lead-based
assumptions.source: Research RF-010; aluminum siding product history
assumptions.note: Factory-baked enamel finish, not lead paint. Even earliest residential aluminum siding (1940s) used baked enamel. EPA RRP does not apply.

assumptions.value: Single finish system for all colors — no LRV-class split, no IR-reflective products needed
assumptions.note: Aluminum conducts heat efficiently — no thermal warping risk at any color. Eliminates LRV-class dimension and IR-reflective material requirement entirely.

assumptions.value: 1 pad per 150 SF — more aggressive than vinyl (1 per 200 SF) due to harder oxide layer
assumptions.source: Research RF-006; researcher analysis of oxide scuff requirements
assumptions.note: Vinyl scuff is for adhesion tooth only; aluminum scuff must break Al2O3 oxide film — more wear on pads. Higher consumption rate. Field calibration recommended.

uncertainty_flags.detail: Three-layer system (self-etch -> epoxy -> acrylic) requires confirmed inter-coat compatibility. Not all epoxy primers are compatible with self-etching primer below and acrylic topcoat above. Product-specific PDS verification needed before specifying coastal variant.
uncertainty_flags.recommendation: Pre-qualify a specific three-product system (self-etch + epoxy + acrylic topcoat from compatible product lines). Document verified system in materials catalog.

uncertainty_flags.topic: Self-etching primer DFT compliance rate in field conditions
uncertainty_flags.detail: Achieving consistent 0.5-1.0 mil DFT with airless spray in field conditions (wind, height, varying angle) is challenging. Over-application risk increases at ladder/scaffold height. Actual field compliance rate is unknown.
uncertainty_flags.recommendation: Scaffold preferred over ladder for multi-story aluminum to improve spray stability. QC spot-checks with DFT gauge. Fine-atomization tips mandatory. Field calibration data needed.

uncertainty_flags.detail: Coverage rates for aluminum shake/shingle profiles are estimated from textured metal surface analogies. Limited manufacturer PDS data specific to aluminum shake panels.
uncertainty_flags.recommendation: Use lower end of range for shake/shingle profiles. Field calibration recommended.

uncertainty_flags.detail: TSP/cleaner consumption for heavy chalk aluminum may exceed 1 EA per 500 SF due to multiple wash passes and higher concentration requirements. Actual consumption depends on chalk severity and number of passes.
uncertainty_flags.recommendation: For heavy chalk severity, estimate 1.5-2x standard cleaner consumption. Budget additional TSP/cleaner for re-wash cycles.
